resources.string: Save your token, then open setup to make this device discoverable.
No Bluetooth adapter (emulator or BT-less device).
Bluetooth is off — enable it first.
This Bluetooth chip can\'t advertise (no peripheral mode), so the Muse app can\'t see us.

Can't pair on this device:

%1$s

Pairing needs a phone/tablet/TV whose Bluetooth chip supports peripheral mode.

Setup open as:

%1$s

On-air Bluetooth name: %2$s
(apps can't rename it; if the Muse app can't find us, rename this device to %1$s in its Bluetooth or device-name settings, then reopen this screen.)

In the Muse app: Settings > Devices > Add Device.

Waiting (10 min window)…
Paired. Start the service below to connect to Muse.
This settings page doesn\'t exist on this device.
Pairing cleared. Pair again to reconnect.
Settings stay on this device. Saving stops the runtime; start it again to apply changes. Use HTTPS or MQTT TLS when available. Plain HTTP and MQTT expose traffic on the local network.
Watch entity IDs (comma-separated; empty watches all)
Subscribe to Home Assistant state events
Forward device events and queued voice messages to Muse

Shell commands run as this app and can access pairing tokens, integration credentials and all app files. Enable only if you trust every command sent by Muse. File workspace restrictions do not isolate an enabled shell.
Saved. Start the service again to apply settings.
Could not start the service. Open the app and check permissions.
Not paired — local controls are available
Tap Listen to start the microphone. Review the transcript before sending. Cloud forwarding must be enabled in Settings. Local actions work without Muse.
The installed speech engine may process audio online. On-device recognition is unavailable.
Local commands: pause / resume / stop, 暫停 / 繼續 / 停止, or scene NAME.
Speech recognition is unavailable. Install or configure a speech engine.
Review the transcript, then choose an action.
Speech recognition ended with error %1$d. You can try again.
The camera is used only while this screen is visible. Tap Take photo to save to the workspace; Analyze reads text and barcodes locally.
Tap Take photo to grant camera access.
Camera unavailable or capture failed. Try reopening this screen.
Repeat every N seconds (optional, at least 60)
Save the current card text. Leave the interval blank to run only on request. Scheduled scenes run locally while the service is running.
Token saved privately. You can now open setup.
A new life for this device.
Show a message. Play something. Put your Android to work.
Display a card on this screen. No Muse pairing needed; just start the service.
Pair once to control this device from your Muse chat. Ask Muse to show a welcome message on this device; use its name if you have several.
Start the service to use local controls or connect to Muse. Your pairing and settings stay saved.
Ready for commands from Muse. Local controls are available here, too.
Local controls are ready. Pair with the Muse phone app when you want remote control.
Local controls remain available while the connection recovers. If this continues, check Wi-Fi and Device → Diagnostics.
Leave a message on screen, or let this device read it aloud.
Play a direct media link or a file saved in this device’s workspace.
Manage integrations and find out what this device can do.
Enter a media URL or workspace file path.
Discover receivers on the same Wi-Fi, then choose where to play.
No Cast receivers found. Check that both devices are on the same Wi-Fi, then try again.
Your next action will appear here. Open result details for the full response.
Request accepted. Check progress to confirm completion.
Response received. Open result details to inspect it.
No launchable apps found on this device.
No saved scenes yet. Add a message and scene ID above, then save your first scene.
Use 1–64 letters, digits, underscores or hyphens.
Use 60–604800 seconds, or leave blank to run manually.
Delete “%1$s”? This removes its schedule and cannot be undone.
Connect this device to your Muse account. Keep the Muse phone app nearby.
Get a token at gadgets.muse.ai → Settings → SDK tokens. It stays in this app’s private storage.
Open setup below. In the Muse phone app, go to Settings → Devices → Add Device.
Invalid SDK token. Copy it again from gadgets.muse.ai.
This device has a saved pairing. You can open controls; only pair again if the connection needs it.
Bluetooth permission is needed to pair. Open setup again to retry, or allow Nearby devices in Android app settings.
Remove the saved Muse pairing? You will need the Muse phone app to pair again. Your SDK token and local settings stay saved.
Device readiness and optional Android settings. Pairing and local controls are available from Home.
Optional. Connect to your own Home Assistant instance. Reading states does not require enabling actions.
Optional. Connect to your broker. Publishing stays off unless you enable it below.
Keep these off until you need them. Camera and microphone still require Android permission and a visible screen.
Settings could not be saved. Please try again.
